missionPremise: hauska-map vendors legacy-design-tools' resolvers, so shared customer-facing strings travel as literals copied between repos, and each repo's pin compares its OWN constant to a literal typed into the SAME repo. The pins describe themselves as making cross-repo drift impossible; measured at source, they cannot see the sibling repo at all, so a one-sided edit that updates the copy's own literal passes both CIs.

existingPins.ruling: KEEP the same-repo pins; do NOT replace them.
existingPins.why: They fail on a different thing from the cross-repo check and fail EARLIER: a lone accidental edit to either copy is caught in that repo's own suite in ~1 minute, before any sibling checkout is involved, and the literal typed in the test is a second, independent statement of the intended value. The cross-repo check is the guard for the edit that updates the local literal too. Two controls failing on different things is the point; leaving both claiming the same thing with different strength was the defect.
existingPins.whatChanged: The comments in all four test files that claimed cross-repo protection now say what the test actually proves (a LOCAL pin) and name scripts/check-cross-repo-literal-drift.mjs as the cross-repo half. No assertion was weakened or deleted; the byte-exact `toBe` comparisons are untouched.

design.check: scripts/check-cross-repo-literal-drift.mjs in hauska-map AND legacy-design-tools, byte-identical (committed bytes sha256 23ae5119976f3d3e6e7f6862e3b441728148ab7ebf9dc0399d265460cc118c2 in both; git blob d366057e5eb0d6109bc0f83d91cc7bdf718b2bfc in both, verified with `git hash-object` on the committed content)
design.howTheValueIsRead: From the DEFINING module on each side - never from a test's copy. `const`/`template`/`disclosure`/`union` kinds are parsed out of the source at the declaration named in the table (import() is not usable: one side is TypeScript in another repo with no build in our job). Parsing is the reason the refusal path exists: if the declaration is renamed or its shape changes, extraction throws DriftRefuse -- exit 2, DRIFT_MARKER_MISSING, never a skip and never a pass.

kinds.const: a `const NAME = <string>` declaration; flags are compared as the literal, pattern and flags separately so a narrowed regex is a diff
kinds.disclosure: the two halves of a composed return (head run + tail run) so an edit in the middle of the sentence is a diff, not a whole-string blob
kinds.template: the string run a function returns, with `${...}` placeholders kept as placeholders
kinds.union: a `type NAME = | ...` union's string-literal members, sorted into a set; a member DROPPED on one side is a diff, and `typeof SOME_CONST` members resolve through the const reader. Members of any other shape (map's `(string & {})` catch-all) are EXCLUDED and the exclusion is stated
kinds.file: sha256 of both copies, CRLF-normalised (the two repos apply different eol attributes on checkout; raw bytes would be a permanent false positive on Windows and would say nothing about the blob)

design.exitTable: 0 PASS / 1 FAIL (values disagree, naming the literal id and both values) / 2 REFUSE (a declaration could not be read where it is expected: renamed, moved, wrong shape, sibling root unreadable) / 3 usage

predictionsOwned: P1: a one-sided edit to any of the 20 literals makes the check exit 1 AND name that literal - in both directions (map drifts, ldt drifts).
P2: the same edit made on both sides exits 0 (the check is not a diff-any-edit alarm).
P3: renaming the defining declaration, or changing its shape from a string expression to something else, exits 2 and never 0 or a skip.
P4: --selftest passes on generated fixtures AND fails when the fixture generator is corrupted (both observed; a control observed only passing has not been observed working).
P5: the sibling's main is what is read in CI - observable because both jobs conclude green on the PRs while the sibling's branch is a different, unrelated branch.
P6: the factory's two literals are watched from the defining side only, and the reverse direction is a NAMED bypass, not a silent gap.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.q: A1 - the check runs in both repos and reads sibling MAIN, so could a green PR check be green because it read its own repo twice?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.disposition: No: the sparse checkout pulls the SIBLING into a separate path and the check is given that root explicitly (--ldt-root ldt-main / --map-root map-main); the local root is the job's workspace. Falsified by violation too: the battery mutates a victim tree and points the check at it, and 24 one-sided cases fail, so the two roots are demonstrably read separately.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.q: A2 - does parsing extract a value from a COMMENT that mentions the literal, i.e. read a mention instead of the definition?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.disposition: This is the failure mode the row names, so it is answered structurally and by measurement. Structurally: extraction starts at a declaration marker (`const NAME =`, `export function NAME(`, `type NAME =`) found by index, then walks to the value; if the marker is missing it REFUSES. By measurement: the battery's marker-scoped mutation found that an earlier battery version was editing a NEIGHBOURING const (`*_FACT_ENTITY_TYPE` one line above `*_FACT_SOURCE`) and the check did not react - which is correct behaviour for the check and a defect in the battery, and it is why every case now names its declaration.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.q: A3 - what happens if the source file cannot be read (sparse checkout misses a path, sibling main lacks the file)?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.disposition: REMOTE_UNREADABLE, exit 2, never exit 0 - readSideFile falls back to `git -C <root> show HEAD:<path>` and refuses if that fails too. This is deliberate: a missing file is exactly the state in which a silent pass would read as 'no drift'.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.q: A4 - the fixture row compares bytes with CRLF normalised. Is that a hole - could two files differ only by line endings and be called identical?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.disposition: Yes, deliberately, and it is stated in the check: the two repos apply different eol attributes on checkout, so the same committed blob lands as CRLF in one tree and LF in the other (measured 5694 vs 5547 bytes for the fixture, exactly the 147 newlines). The claim the row makes is about the BLOB, and normalising is what makes the comparison say that. A file with different CONTENT that differs only in line endings' placement is a diff.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.q: A5 - why is the row list 20 and not 'everything'? What keeps a 21st copy from going unwatched?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.disposition: Nothing keeps it, and that is the first named bypass in the check's header: the table IS the enumeration. The trigger to add a row is any comment in either repo claiming a copy - which is now a deliberately conspicuous marker, because the P-331 defect was a comment claiming a control that did not exist. The two rows this lane deliberately did NOT add are handed over in leave_behind with the exact reason.
